q25168.en: Grip allows the vehicle to move.

explain.short: The wheels push on the road thanks to grip. Without grip the wheels just spin and the car does not move.
explain.rule: Grip (forza aderente) is the friction between tyres and road. Without it the car cannot move, steer or brake, and it slides.
explain.trap: 'consente il movimento' (allows movement) is correct: grip turns the wheel's turning into forward motion.

sceneParams.caption: Grip lets the wheels push the car forward
lines: Wheels turn and push on the road
No grip: wheels spin, car stays

q25169.en: Grip resists sliding towards the outside of the bend.

explain.short: In a bend a force pushes the car outwards. Grip between tyres and road holds the car on its line.
explain.rule: Grip (forza aderente) is the friction between tyres and road. Without it the car cannot move, steer or brake, and it slides.
explain.trap: 'verso l'esterno della curva' (towards the outside of the bend) is the right direction of the slide.

sceneParams.caption: Grip holds the car in the bend
lines: In a bend the car is pushed outwards
Grip holds the tyres on the road
The car stays on its line

keywords.en: towards the outside of the bend

q25170.en: Grip allows the vehicle to follow the path it wants.

explain.short: When you steer, the tyres need grip to change the car's direction. With grip the car goes where you steer it.
explain.rule: Grip (forza aderente) is the friction between tyres and road. Without it the car cannot move, steer or brake, and it slides.
explain.trap: 'traiettoria voluta' (the wanted path) is correct: grip makes steering work.

sceneParams.caption: Grip lets the car go where you steer

q25171.en: Grip resists the tyre slipping on the asphalt.

explain.short: Grip is the friction between tyre and asphalt. Friction is exactly what stops the tyre from slipping.
explain.rule: Grip (forza aderente) is the friction between tyres and road. Without it the car cannot move, steer or brake, and it slides.
explain.trap: 'slittamento dello pneumatico' (tyre slipping) is what grip is there to stop.

sceneParams.caption: Grip stops the tyre slipping

q25172.en: Grip does not resist sliding caused by side wind.

explain.short: Grip resists every slide, whatever the cause. A strong side wind pushes the car sideways, and grip holds it.
explain.rule: Grip (forza aderente) is the friction between tyres and road. Without it the car cannot move, steer or brake, and it slides.
explain.trap: 'non si oppone' (does not resist) is wrong: grip fights the slide from the wind too.

sceneParams.caption: Grip also holds the car against side wind
lines: Side wind pushes the car sideways
Grip holds the tyres on the road
Saying it does not help: wrong

q25173.en: Grip, if too high, causes the brakes to overheat.

explain.short: Grip is between the tyres and the road. Brakes overheat from long or hard use, for example on long downhill roads, not from grip.
explain.rule: Grip (forza aderente) is the friction between tyres and road. Without it the car cannot move, steer or brake, and it slides.
explain.trap: 'surriscaldamento dei freni' (brakes overheating) has nothing to do with grip.

sceneParams.caption: Hot brakes come from long braking, not grip

q25174.en: Grip increases if the asphalt is rough.

explain.short: A rough surface gives the tyre more to hold on to. So the tyre grips better than on smooth asphalt.
explain.rule: Grip is highest on dry, clean, rough asphalt. Wet roads, leaves, ice, mud and oil reduce it.
explain.trap: 'rugoso' (rough) is good for grip, not bad.

sceneParams.caption: Rough asphalt gives more grip

q25175.en: Grip decreases if the asphalt is wet.

explain.short: Water makes a thin layer between tyre and road. The tyre holds less, so grip goes down.
explain.rule: Grip is highest on dry, clean, rough asphalt. Wet roads, leaves, ice, mud and oil reduce it.
explain.trap: 'diminuisce' (decreases) with 'bagnato' (wet) is the correct pair.

sceneParams.caption: Wet asphalt means less grip

q25176.en: Grip increases if the asphalt is wet.

explain.short: Water between the tyre and the road makes the tyre hold less. Grip goes down, not up.
explain.rule: Grip is highest on dry, clean, rough asphalt. Wet roads, leaves, ice, mud and oil reduce it.
explain.trap: 'aumenta' (increases) is wrong: on wet asphalt grip 'diminuisce' (decreases).

sceneParams.caption: Wet asphalt lowers grip, it does not raise it
lines: Slow down and keep more distance

q25177.en: Grip increases if the asphalt is covered with leaves.

explain.short: Leaves on the road are slippery, especially when wet. They lower grip, they do not raise it.
explain.rule: Grip is highest on dry, clean, rough asphalt. Wet roads, leaves, ice, mud and oil reduce it.
explain.trap: 'aumenta' (increases) is wrong: leaves ('foglie') make the road slippery.

sceneParams.caption: Leaves make the road slippery

q25178.en: Grip increases if the asphalt is covered with ice.

explain.short: Ice is the most slippery surface of all. Grip becomes very low.
explain.rule: Grip is highest on dry, clean, rough asphalt. Wet roads, leaves, ice, mud and oil reduce it.
explain.trap: 'aumenta' (increases) is wrong: on 'ghiaccio' (ice) grip is very low.

sceneParams.caption: Ice gives very little grip

q25179.en: Grip increases if the asphalt is covered with mud.

explain.short: Mud is soft and slippery between tyre and road. It lowers grip.
explain.rule: Grip is highest on dry, clean, rough asphalt. Wet roads, leaves, ice, mud and oil reduce it.
explain.trap: 'aumenta' (increases) is wrong: 'fango' (mud) makes the road slippery.

sceneParams.caption: Mud makes the road slippery

q25180.en: If the grip coefficient decreases, the driving wheels could spin.

explain.short: The driving wheels (ruote motrici) push the car. With little grip they cannot push on the road and spin on the spot.
explain.rule: A low grip coefficient makes the car slide more and brake in a longer space. You must drive slower everywhere.
explain.trap: 'pattinare' (spin, slip) is what driving wheels do on a slippery road.

sceneParams.caption: Low grip: driving wheels can spin
lines: Driving wheels spin on the spot

q25181.en: If the grip coefficient decreases, the braking distance increases.

explain.short: With less grip the brakes cannot slow the car as fast. The car needs more road to stop.
explain.rule: A low grip coefficient makes the car slide more and brake in a longer space. You must drive slower everywhere.
explain.trap: 'aumenta' (increases) is correct here: less grip, longer braking.

sceneParams.caption: Low grip: longer braking distance

q25182.en: If the grip coefficient is low, you must reduce speed.

explain.short: On a slippery road the car slides and stops later. Lower speed gives you back control and space.
explain.rule: A low grip coefficient makes the car slide more and brake in a longer space. You must drive slower everywhere.
explain.trap: 'bisogna ridurre la velocità' (you must slow down): no 'solo' (only), so it is right.

sceneParams.caption: Low grip: slow down

q25183.en: If the grip coefficient decreases, the braking distance gets shorter.

explain.short: Less grip means the brakes hold the car less. The car needs MORE road to stop, not less.
explain.rule: A low grip coefficient makes the car slide more and brake in a longer space. You must drive slower everywhere.
explain.trap: 'si riduce' (gets shorter) is wrong: the braking distance 'aumenta' (gets longer).

sceneParams.caption: Low grip makes braking LONGER

q25184.en: If the grip coefficient is low, you must reduce speed only in bends.

explain.short: Low grip is a danger everywhere: on straights you also brake later and can skid. You must slow down always.
explain.rule: A low grip coefficient makes the car slide more and brake in a longer space. You must drive slower everywhere.
explain.trap: 'solo in curva' (only in bends) is the trap: you slow down everywhere.

sceneParams.caption: Low grip: slow down everywhere, not only in bends

q25185.en: A low grip coefficient limits the speed at which you can drive through a bend safely.

explain.short: In a bend grip holds the car against the outward push. With little grip the car slides at a lower speed, so the safe bend speed is lower.
explain.rule: A low grip coefficient makes the car slide more and brake in a longer space. You must drive slower everywhere.
explain.trap: 'limita la velocità' (limits the speed) is correct: low grip means a slower safe speed in the bend.

sceneParams.caption: Low grip: take the bend slower
lines: Slippery road and a bend ahead

q25186.en: A low grip coefficient makes sliding in a bend more likely.

explain.short: In a bend the car is pushed outwards and only grip holds it. With low grip the tyres let go more easily.
explain.rule: A low grip coefficient makes the car slide more and brake in a longer space. You must drive slower everywhere.
explain.trap: 'favorisce' (makes more likely) is correct: low grip helps the skid happen.

sceneParams.caption: Low grip: easier to slide in a bend

q25187.en: A low grip coefficient increases the braking distance.

explain.short: With little grip the brakes slow the car less. The car needs more road to stop.
explain.rule: A low grip coefficient makes the car slide more and brake in a longer space. You must drive slower everywhere.
explain.trap: 'aumenta' (increases) is correct: low grip, longer braking.

sceneParams.caption: Low grip: longer braking distance

q25188.en: A low grip coefficient makes sudden braking dangerous.

explain.short: Braking hard on a slippery road can lock the wheels and make the car skid. Brake gently and early.
explain.rule: A low grip coefficient makes the car slide more and brake in a longer space. You must drive slower everywhere.
explain.trap: 'frenate brusche' (sudden braking) is exactly what is risky with low grip.

sceneParams.caption: Low grip: brake gently, not suddenly

q25189.en: A low grip coefficient does not affect the vehicle's speed.

explain.short: With low grip you must drive slower, because you brake later and slide more easily. So it does affect speed.
explain.rule: A low grip coefficient makes the car slide more and brake in a longer space. You must drive slower everywhere.
explain.trap: 'non condiziona' (does not affect) is wrong: low grip forces you to slow down.

sceneParams.caption: Low grip forces you to drive slower

q25190.en: A low grip coefficient reduces the braking distance.

explain.short: Low grip makes the brakes less effective. The braking distance gets longer, not shorter.
explain.rule: A low grip coefficient makes the car slide more and brake in a longer space. You must drive slower everywhere.
explain.trap: 'riduce' (reduces) is wrong: low grip 'aumenta' (increases) the braking distance.

sceneParams.caption: Low grip makes braking LONGER

q25191.en: A low grip coefficient lowers fuel consumption.

explain.short: Grip is about holding the road, not about saving fuel. If anything, spinning wheels waste fuel.
explain.rule: A low grip coefficient makes the car slide more and brake in a longer space. You must drive slower everywhere.
explain.trap: 'diminuisce i consumi' (lowers fuel use) is an invented benefit.

sceneParams.caption: Low grip does not save fuel
lines: Low grip: car holds the road less

q25192.en: A low grip coefficient reduces sliding in a bend.

explain.short: Low grip means the tyres hold the road less. Sliding in a bend becomes MORE likely, not less.
explain.rule: A low grip coefficient makes the car slide more and brake in a longer space. You must drive slower everywhere.
explain.trap: 'riduce' (reduces) is wrong: low grip 'favorisce' (makes more likely) the slide.

sceneParams.caption: Low grip makes sliding in bends MORE likely

q25193.en: Anyone riding a motorcycle must consider that grip decreases on rails, especially in the rain.

explain.short: Metal rails are smooth. When wet they are very slippery for the thin tyres of a motorcycle.
explain.rule: On a motorcycle grip depends on the surface: rails and road paint are slippery, above all when wet.
explain.trap: 'specialmente in caso di pioggia' (especially in the rain) is correct: rails are worst when wet.

sceneParams.caption: Rails are slippery, above all in rain

q25194.en: Anyone riding a motorcycle must consider that grip decreases on the road markings in the rain.

explain.short: The paint of the road markings is smoother than asphalt. When wet it becomes slippery for a motorcycle.
explain.rule: On a motorcycle grip depends on the surface: rails and road paint are slippery, above all when wet.
explain.trap: 'strisce della segnaletica orizzontale' (painted road markings) are slippery when wet.

sceneParams.caption: Wet road paint is slippery for motorbikes
lines: In the rain they are slippery
Less grip: avoid braking on them

q25195.en: A motorcycle rider must consider that grip does not depend on the type of road surface.

explain.short: Grip changes a lot with the surface: asphalt, cobblestones, rails, paint, gravel. So it does depend on it.
explain.rule: On a motorcycle grip depends on the surface: rails and road paint are slippery, above all when wet.
explain.trap: 'non dipende' (does not depend) is wrong: the surface is one of the main factors.

sceneParams.caption: Grip depends on the road surface

q25196.en: Anyone riding a motorcycle must consider that grip decreases when carrying a passenger.

explain.short: A passenger adds weight and changes how the bike handles, but it does not make the tyres hold the road less.
explain.rule: On a motorcycle grip depends on the surface: rails and road paint are slippery, above all when wet.
explain.trap: 'quando trasporta un passeggero' (when carrying a passenger) is not a cause of lower grip.

sceneParams.caption: A passenger does not reduce grip
lines: Grip depends on road and tyres

q25197.en: Grip decreases if the road is dirty with oil.

explain.short: Oil makes a slippery film on the asphalt. The tyre cannot hold, so grip goes down.
explain.rule: Grip depends on the road (dry and clean is best; oil, ice, mud are bad) and on the tyres, including their pressure.
explain.trap: 'sporca di olio' (dirty with oil) is one of the most slippery conditions.

sceneParams.caption: Oil on the road lowers grip

q25198.en: Grip is greater if the asphalt is dry and clean.

explain.short: Nothing lies between the tyre and the road. This is when the tyre holds best.
explain.rule: Grip depends on the road (dry and clean is best; oil, ice, mud are bad) and on the tyres, including their pressure.
explain.trap: 'asciutto e pulito' (dry and clean) is the best case for grip.

sceneParams.caption: Dry, clean asphalt: best grip

q25199.en: Grip increases if the asphalt is covered with ice.

explain.short: Ice is the most slippery surface of all. Grip becomes very low.
explain.rule: Grip depends on the road (dry and clean is best; oil, ice, mud are bad) and on the tyres, including their pressure.
explain.trap: 'aumenta' (increases) is wrong: on 'ghiaccio' (ice) grip is very low.

sceneParams.caption: Ice gives very little grip

q25200.en: Grip increases if the asphalt is covered with mud.

explain.short: Mud is soft and slippery between tyre and road. It lowers grip.
explain.rule: Grip depends on the road (dry and clean is best; oil, ice, mud are bad) and on the tyres, including their pressure.
explain.trap: 'aumenta' (increases) is wrong: 'fango' (mud) makes the road slippery.

sceneParams.caption: Mud makes the road slippery

q25201.en: Grip does not depend on tyre pressure.

explain.short: Tyre pressure changes how much of the tyre touches the road. Wrong pressure lowers grip, so grip does depend on it.
explain.rule: Grip depends on the road (dry and clean is best; oil, ice, mud are bad) and on the tyres, including their pressure.
explain.trap: 'non dipende' (does not depend) is wrong: pressure affects grip.

sceneParams.caption: Correct tyre pressure is needed for grip
lines: Tyre pressure too low or too high

q25202.en: When the vehicle drives through a bend, it is subject to a force that tends to push it outwards.

explain.short: In a bend the car wants to keep going straight. This pushes it towards the outside of the bend (centrifugal force).
explain.rule: In a bend the car is pushed outwards. Too much speed makes it skid or roll over, so slow down before the bend.
explain.trap: 'verso l'esterno' (outwards) is the correct direction.

sceneParams.caption: In a bend the car is pushed outwards
lines: Grip holds it on the road

q25203.en: When the vehicle drives through a bend, too much speed can make it skid.

explain.short: The faster you go, the stronger the outward push. If it is stronger than the grip, the car skids.
explain.rule: In a bend the car is pushed outwards. Too much speed makes it skid or roll over, so slow down before the bend.
explain.trap: 'velocità eccessiva' (too much speed) and 'sbandamento' (skid) go together.

sceneParams.caption: Too fast in a bend: the car skids
lines: The car skids: slow down first

q25204.en: When the vehicle drives through a bend, too much speed can make it roll over.

explain.short: At high speed the outward push can be so strong that the car tips over, above all if it is tall or loaded high.
explain.rule: In a bend the car is pushed outwards. Too much speed makes it skid or roll over, so slow down before the bend.
explain.trap: 'ribaltamento' (rolling over) is a real risk of too much speed in a bend.

sceneParams.caption: Too fast in a bend: the car can roll over

q25205.en: When the vehicle drives through a bend, it is subject to a force that tends to push it inwards.

explain.short: The force in a bend pushes the car towards the OUTSIDE, not the inside.
explain.rule: In a bend the car is pushed outwards. Too much speed makes it skid or roll over, so slow down before the bend.
explain.trap: 'verso l'interno' (inwards) is wrong: the push is 'verso l'esterno' (outwards).

sceneParams.caption: The push in a bend is outwards, not inwards

q25206.en: When the vehicle drives through a bend, you must increase speed to avoid sliding.

explain.short: More speed makes the outward push stronger and a slide MORE likely. You slow down before the bend.
explain.rule: In a bend the car is pushed outwards. Too much speed makes it skid or roll over, so slow down before the bend.
explain.trap: 'aumentare la velocità' (increase speed) is the opposite of the right thing.

sceneParams.caption: Speeding up in a bend makes sliding worse

q25207.en: When the vehicle drives through a bend, you must increase speed to avoid rolling over.

explain.short: The rollover force grows with speed. Going faster makes rolling over MORE likely.
explain.rule: In a bend the car is pushed outwards. Too much speed makes it skid or roll over, so slow down before the bend.
explain.trap: 'aumentare la velocità' (increase speed) is wrong: you must slow down.

sceneParams.caption: Speeding up in a bend risks rollover

q25208.en: A vehicle rolling over in a bend is made more likely by a load placed high up.

explain.short: A high load raises the centre of gravity (the balance point). In a bend the vehicle tips over more easily.
explain.rule: High or loose loads, a narrow track and a tight bend make a rollover more likely. Low loads, a wide track and wide bends make the vehicle more stable.
explain.trap: 'carico posto in alto' (load placed high) is bad for stability.

sceneParams.caption: High load: easier rollover
lines: Easier to tip over in a bend

q25209.en: A vehicle rolling over in a bend is made more likely by a load that is not firmly secured.

explain.short: A loose load slides to the outside in a bend. This sudden shift of weight can tip the vehicle over.
explain.rule: High or loose loads, a narrow track and a tight bend make a rollover more likely. Low loads, a wide track and wide bends make the vehicle more stable.
explain.trap: 'non stabilmente fissato' (not firmly secured) is dangerous: the load moves in the bend.

sceneParams.caption: Loose load: easier rollover
lines: In the bend it slides outwards

q25210.en: A vehicle rolling over in a bend is made more likely by a small distance between the wheels of the same axle (narrow track).

explain.short: Wheels close together give a narrow base. A narrow base tips over more easily than a wide one.
explain.rule: High or loose loads, a narrow track and a tight bend make a rollover more likely. Low loads, a wide track and wide bends make the vehicle more stable.
explain.trap: 'carreggiata stretta' (narrow track) here means the vehicle's wheels, not the road.

sceneParams.caption: Narrow track: easier rollover
lines: Wheels of one axle close together
Easier to tip over in a bend

keywords.it: ridotta distanza fra ruote dello stesso asse
keywords.en: small distance between wheels of the same axle

q25211.en: A vehicle rolling over in a bend is made more likely by a small road curve radius (tight bend).

explain.short: In a tight bend the car turns sharply and the outward push is stronger. So the risk of rolling over is higher.
explain.rule: High or loose loads, a narrow track and a tight bend make a rollover more likely. Low loads, a wide track and wide bends make the vehicle more stable.
explain.trap: 'raggio piccolo' (small radius) means a TIGHT bend, which is the dangerous one.

sceneParams.caption: Tight bend: easier rollover

q25212.en: A vehicle rolling over in a bend is made more likely by a large distance between the wheels of the same axle (wide track).

explain.short: A wide track gives the vehicle a wide base. A wide base makes it MORE stable, not less.
explain.rule: High or loose loads, a narrow track and a tight bend make a rollover more likely. Low loads, a wide track and wide bends make the vehicle more stable.
explain.trap: 'carreggiata larga' (wide track) helps stability; the narrow one is the danger.

sceneParams.caption: Wide track makes the vehicle more stable
lines: Wheels of one axle far apart

keywords.it: ampia distanza fra ruote dello stesso asse
keywords.en: large distance between wheels of the same axle

q25213.en: A vehicle rolling over in a bend is made more likely by a load placed low down.

explain.short: A low load keeps the centre of gravity (balance point) low. This makes the vehicle MORE stable.
explain.rule: High or loose loads, a narrow track and a tight bend make a rollover more likely. Low loads, a wide track and wide bends make the vehicle more stable.
explain.trap: 'carico posto in basso' (load placed low) is the safe position; high loads are the danger.

sceneParams.caption: Low load makes the vehicle more stable

q25214.en: A vehicle rolling over in a bend is made more likely by a large road curve radius (wide bend).

explain.short: A wide bend turns gently and the outward push is weaker. The dangerous one is the tight bend.
explain.rule: High or loose loads, a narrow track and a tight bend make a rollover more likely. Low loads, a wide track and wide bends make the vehicle more stable.
explain.trap: 'raggio ampio' (large radius) means a WIDE, gentle bend: less risk, not more.

sceneParams.caption: Wide bend: less risk of rollover

q25215.en: The rollover force in a bend increases as speed increases.

explain.short: The faster you go into a bend, the harder the vehicle is pushed outwards. So the rollover force grows.
explain.rule: The rollover force in a bend grows with speed.
explain.trap: 'aumenta all'aumentare' (increases as ... increases) is the correct link.

sceneParams.caption: Faster in a bend: stronger rollover force

q25216.en: The rollover force in a bend decreases as speed increases.

explain.short: More speed pushes the vehicle outwards harder. The rollover force grows, it does not shrink.
explain.rule: The rollover force in a bend grows with speed.
explain.trap: 'diminuisce' (decreases) is wrong: it 'aumenta' (increases) with speed.

sceneParams.caption: Rollover force grows with speed

q25217.en: ABS prevents the wheels from locking.

explain.short: When you brake hard, ABS lets go of the brake on a wheel for a moment if it starts to lock. So the wheels keep turning.
explain.rule: ABS stops any wheel from locking during braking, so you can still steer and use the maximum grip.
explain.trap: 'impedisce alle ruote di bloccarsi' (prevents the wheels from locking) is exactly ABS's job.

sceneParams.caption: ABS keeps the wheels from locking

q25218.en: ABS lets you correct the vehicle's path even during emergency braking.

explain.short: A locked wheel cannot steer. Because ABS keeps the wheels turning, you can still steer around an obstacle while braking.
explain.rule: ABS stops any wheel from locking during braking, so you can still steer and use the maximum grip.
explain.trap: 'anche durante una frenata di emergenza' (even during emergency braking) is correct with ABS.

sceneParams.caption: With ABS you can steer while braking hard

q25219.en: ABS lets you use the maximum grip when braking.

explain.short: A tyre that is still rolling grips better than a locked, sliding tyre. ABS keeps each wheel just before locking, where grip is highest.
explain.rule: ABS stops any wheel from locking during braking, so you can still steer and use the maximum grip.
explain.trap: 'massima forza aderente' (maximum grip) is what ABS lets you use.

sceneParams.caption: ABS uses the maximum grip when braking

q25220.en: ABS can act on all the wheels, working each time on the ones that are about to lock during braking.

explain.short: ABS has a sensor on every wheel. It works only on the wheel that is about to lock, at that moment.
explain.rule: ABS stops any wheel from locking during braking, so you can still steer and use the maximum grip.
explain.trap: 'di volta in volta' (each time) means ABS acts wheel by wheel, as needed.

sceneParams.caption: ABS watches every wheel

q25221.en: ABS also works when the tyres are worn.

explain.short: ABS is part of the braking system, not of the tyres. It still works with worn tyres, but worn tyres have less grip, so you brake worse anyway.
explain.rule: ABS stops any wheel from locking during braking, so you can still steer and use the maximum grip.
explain.trap: 'anche quando' (also when) is correct: ABS keeps working, but it cannot fix worn tyres.

sceneParams.caption: ABS works with worn tyres too

q25222.en: ABS also works when the asphalt is wet.

explain.short: On wet asphalt the wheels lock more easily, so ABS is especially useful there. It works on any road surface.
explain.rule: ABS stops any wheel from locking during braking, so you can still steer and use the maximum grip.
explain.trap: 'anche quando l'asfalto è bagnato' (also on wet asphalt) is correct.

sceneParams.caption: ABS works on wet roads too

q25223.en: ABS makes braking safer because it prevents the wheels from locking.

explain.short: Wheels that do not lock keep their grip and let you steer. That is why braking with ABS is safer.
explain.rule: ABS stops any wheel from locking during braking, so you can still steer and use the maximum grip.
explain.trap: 'più sicura' (safer) with the reason 'impedisce alle ruote di bloccarsi' is correct.

sceneParams.caption: ABS: safer braking, no locked wheels

q25224.en: ABS makes it easier for the wheels to lock.

explain.short: ABS does the opposite: it stops the wheels from locking.
explain.rule: ABS stops any wheel from locking during braking, so you can still steer and use the maximum grip.
explain.trap: 'favorisce il bloccaggio' (makes locking easier) is the opposite of what ABS does.

sceneParams.caption: ABS PREVENTS wheel locking

q25225.en: ABS prevents you from changing the vehicle's path during braking.

explain.short: ABS keeps the wheels turning, so you CAN steer while braking. It does not stop you steering.
explain.rule: ABS stops any wheel from locking during braking, so you can still steer and use the maximum grip.
explain.trap: 'impedisce di modificare la traiettoria' (prevents changing the path) is wrong: ABS makes steering possible.

sceneParams.caption: With ABS you CAN steer while braking

q25226.en: ABS prevents you from using the maximum grip when braking.

explain.short: ABS keeps each wheel just before locking, where grip is highest. So it lets you use the maximum grip.
explain.rule: ABS stops any wheel from locking during braking, so you can still steer and use the maximum grip.
explain.trap: 'impedisce' (prevents) is wrong: ABS 'consente' (allows) the maximum grip.

sceneParams.caption: ABS lets you USE the maximum grip
lines: ABS keeps the wheels at best grip

q25227.en: ABS does not act on the driving wheels.

explain.short: ABS works on ALL wheels, driving wheels (ruote motrici) included.
explain.rule: ABS stops any wheel from locking during braking, so you can still steer and use the maximum grip.
explain.trap: 'non agisce sulle ruote motrici' (does not act on driving wheels) is wrong: it acts on every wheel.

sceneParams.caption: ABS works on ALL wheels
lines: ABS has a sensor on every wheel

q25228.en: ABS does not switch on if the tyres are worn.

explain.short: ABS is part of the brakes and works whatever the state of the tyres. Worn tyres reduce grip, but ABS still switches on.
explain.rule: ABS stops any wheel from locking during braking, so you can still steer and use the maximum grip.
explain.trap: 'non si attiva' (does not switch on) is wrong: ABS works with worn tyres too.

sceneParams.caption: ABS works with worn tyres too

q25229.en: You must check the tyre inflation pressure regularly, including that of the spare wheel.

explain.short: Tyres slowly lose air. The spare wheel too: if you need it and it is flat, it is useless.
explain.rule: Check the pressure often, with cold tyres, spare wheel included, and adapt it to the load.
explain.trap: 'compresa quella della ruota di scorta' (including the spare wheel) is correct.

sceneParams.caption: Check pressure often, spare wheel too

q25230.en: Tyre inflation pressure must be adapted to the weight conditions of the vehicle.

explain.short: A heavily loaded car needs more pressure than an empty one. The car's manual gives values for both.
explain.rule: Check the pressure often, with cold tyres, spare wheel included, and adapt it to the load.
explain.trap: 'adeguata alle condizioni di peso' (adapted to the weight) is correct.

sceneParams.caption: Adapt tyre pressure to the load
lines: Car full of people and luggage
Adapt the pressure to the load

q25231.en: The correct tyre inflation pressure depends on the vehicle's load and on the number of passengers carried.

explain.short: More passengers and luggage mean more weight on the tyres. So the right pressure changes with the load.
explain.rule: Check the pressure often, with cold tyres, spare wheel included, and adapt it to the load.
explain.trap: 'carico' (load) and 'numero dei passeggeri' (number of passengers) are both correct factors.

sceneParams.caption: Pressure depends on load and passengers
lines: Set the pressure for that load

q25232.en: Too low tyre inflation pressure increases friction and also fuel consumption.

explain.short: A soft tyre flattens more on the road and rolls with more effort. The engine works harder and uses more fuel.
explain.rule: Check the pressure often, with cold tyres, spare wheel included, and adapt it to the load.
explain.trap: 'insufficiente' (too low) pressure: more friction and more fuel, both correct.

sceneParams.caption: Low pressure: more friction, more fuel

q25233.en: Tyre inflation pressure must be checked when the tyre is cold.

explain.short: Driving heats the tyre and the air inside expands, so the pressure reads higher. Only a cold tyre gives the true value.
explain.rule: Check the pressure often, with cold tyres, spare wheel included, and adapt it to the load.
explain.trap: 'fredda' (cold) is correct; a hot tyre gives a wrong reading.

sceneParams.caption: Check pressure with cold tyres
lines: Hot tyres give a wrong value

q25234.en: The automatic tyre pressure monitoring system increases the safety of vehicles fitted with it.

explain.short: The system warns you on the dashboard when a tyre loses pressure. You can act before it becomes dangerous.
explain.rule: Check the pressure often, with cold tyres, spare wheel included, and adapt it to the load.
explain.trap: 'fa aumentare la sicurezza' (increases safety) is correct.

sceneParams.caption: Pressure monitor warns you: more safety
lines: Warning light if a tyre loses air

q25235.en: If you measure tyre inflation pressure when the tyre is hot, you get a correct reading of the pressure values.

explain.short: A hot tyre has a higher pressure than normal. The reading is wrong; measure with cold tyres.
explain.rule: Check the pressure often, with cold tyres, spare wheel included, and adapt it to the load.
explain.trap: 'calda' (hot) is the trap: the correct reading is with the tyre 'fredda' (cold).

sceneParams.caption: Hot tyres give a wrong pressure reading

q25236.en: Tyre inflation pressure should be checked after driving a few kilometres, as soon as the tyre has heated up.

explain.short: Heat makes the pressure read higher. You check it with cold tyres, before driving.
explain.rule: Check the pressure often, with cold tyres, spare wheel included, and adapt it to the load.
explain.trap: 'appena la gomma si è surriscaldata' (as soon as the tyre is hot) is the wrong moment.

sceneParams.caption: Check pressure cold, not after driving
lines: After a few km the tyre is hot

q25237.en: Tyre inflation pressure should be set according to the material of the wheel rims (steel, light alloy, etc.).

explain.short: The right pressure depends on the car, the tyres and the load. The rim material does not matter.
explain.rule: Check the pressure often, with cold tyres, spare wheel included, and adapt it to the load.
explain.trap: 'cerchioni' (wheel rims) is an invented factor.

sceneParams.caption: Rim material does not decide the pressure

q25238.en: Before starting a long journey, it is a good idea to increase the tyre inflation pressure.

explain.short: You check that the pressure is the right one, not higher. Too much pressure reduces the tyre's contact with the road and its grip.
explain.rule: Check the pressure often, with cold tyres, spare wheel included, and adapt it to the load.
explain.trap: 'aumentare' (increase) is the trap: you check and set the correct value, you do not raise it.

sceneParams.caption: Before a trip: check pressure, do not raise it

q25239.en: In vehicles with a trailer, the tyre inflation pressure of the towing vehicle must be the same as that of the trailer's tyres.

explain.short: The car and the trailer have different tyres and loads. Each one has its own correct pressure.
explain.rule: Check the pressure often, with cold tyres, spare wheel included, and adapt it to the load.
explain.trap: 'uguale' (the same) is wrong: each vehicle uses its own pressure values.

sceneParams.caption: Car and trailer have their own pressures
